missionPremise: The kit gives .pill, .prov (inline-flex), .state and .metric (flex) an explicit display, so the user-agent [hidden] rule loses and el.hidden = true is inert. Source: web/shell.css lines 104/122/259/296 on base 23154be, and the G-76 to G-79 close at _inbox/2026-08-18_g76_g79_fixture_city_and_type.md which records the shipped defect (amber Partial pill beside 'no meeting packet has been read') and names the root fix as one [hidden] rule in shell.css.

designDecision.placement: web/shell.css, immediately after the base reset, before the type block. Placement is deliberately irrelevant to correctness; that is the property being bought.
designDecision.specificityReasoning: An attribute selector and a class each score (0,1,0). [hidden] and .pill therefore tie and source order decides, which is why the UA rule loses today. Raising selector weight only moves the tie: [hidden][hidden] is (0,2,0), which beats one class but ties .lens.on and .shell-nav.open (both (0,2,0), source order again) and loses to any future three-class rule. Placing the rule last in the file is the same bet in different clothing. An important author declaration is the only form that outranks every normal author declaration regardless of specificity, regardless of position in the file, and regardless of a normal inline style attribute, so the rule holds without knowing anything about the rest of the stylesheet. That is exactly the requirement the card sets: hold wherever a future component rule lands.
designDecision.exclusionSet: hidden="until-found" is carved out because the UA sheet gives that value content-visibility: hidden, not display: none. Forcing display: none on it would silently change platform semantics (find-in-page reveal). Measured: zero occurrences of until-found in web/ and src/ on base 23154be, so the carve-out changes nothing today and prevents a surprise later.
rejected: [hidden][hidden] { display: none } — (0,2,0), still a source-order bet against .lens.on and .shell-nav.open, loses to a future three-class rule
html [hidden] { display: none } — (0,1,1), loses to any two-class rule
rule placed last in the file — correctness depends on nobody appending a component rule after it, which is the failure mode this card retires
@layer wrapping of the component rules — would work, but restructures the whole stylesheet and sc-kit.css, far outside a card scoped to one display rule plus two deletions
